title: SceneGraph
description: The intermediate representation produced once per location. Coordinates are meters in a local ENU frame, x east, y north, origin (0,0) at the requested center. Never lat/lon past this boundary.

Ring.description: Closed polygon ring as a list of [x, y] points. Exterior rings CCW, hole rings CW.

name.description: schema_version 4, OPTIONAL. The OSM `name` tag, verbatim. Absent when the element carries none, and absent for the smallest footprints when the ingest's name budget is exceeded (apps/web/lib/engine/osm/normalize.ts).

osm_id.description: schema_version 4, OPTIONAL. The source OSM element id, "w123" or "r456". `id` is unique within the SceneGraph and gains a "-N" suffix when one element produced several parts; this is the unsuffixed source, so two parts of one building name the same element. ABSENT means `id` is already the source id, which is the common case; writing the duplicate out cost 11 % of the Chicago payload.

kind.description: schema_version 4, OPTIONAL. The OSM tag that classified this entity, as "key=value": "building=apartments", "building=yes".

name.description: schema_version 4, OPTIONAL. The OSM `name` tag, verbatim, e.g. "West Adams Street".

osm_id.description: schema_version 4, OPTIONAL. The source OSM way id, unsuffixed; `id` gains a "-N" suffix per clipped segment. ABSENT means `id` is already the source id.

kind.description: schema_version 4, OPTIONAL. The OSM tag that classified this road, as "key=value": "highway=trunk", "highway=footway". `class` is the six-member printing bucket this was mapped into; `kind` is the raw tag, and is written ONLY where the two differ. ABSENT means the raw tag was exactly "highway=" + class, which is lossless and is what keeps the identity block off the transfer budget on a road-dense scene.

name.description: schema_version 4, OPTIONAL. The OSM `name` tag of the element this polygon came from, e.g. "Lake Michigan", "Grant Park".

osm_id.description: schema_version 4, OPTIONAL. The source OSM element id. Water and green polygons are DISSOLVED across elements that overlap or share a boundary node, so this names the largest contributor to this polygon, not its only one.

kind.description: schema_version 4, OPTIONAL. The OSM tag that classified this polygon, as "key=value": "natural=water", "waterway=riverbank", "landuse=grass", "leisure=park".
